_why: EMPTY, and that is the finished state — not a check that was switched
off. Ticket 86bbq065f straightened every panel in here on 2026-09-08.
What this file records: panels whose shared chrome and stacked settings
column do NOT share one left edge. It arrived with 32 names on it
(86bbw8643, 2026-09-07) because asserting the seam outright would have
left check:panels red for every other lane until the fix landed, and a
permanently red gate is one everybody learns to ignore.
The fix, in one line: the shared chrome is rendered INTO the first
settings column and flattened, so the chrome's labels and controls are
grid items of that column and `max-content` measures both halves at once.
Mechanism and why it is a slot rather than a CSS rule:
components/builder/builder-module-chrome-slot.tsx.
THE ASSERTION DID NOT GO AWAY WITH THE LIST, and that distinction is the
whole reason to read this. check_panels measures a merged panel by
comparing the chrome's own rows against the column's other rows, so a
panel that stops sharing the lattice — the flattening removed, a new
settings panel that renders no `BuilderModuleChromeSlot`, a chrome left
outside every column — fails on its own name. It was broken on purpose
and watched to fail before this file was emptied; the PR says what was
broken.
So an addition here is a REGRESSION being recorded, never an exemption.
The rule the check enforces is unchanged and runs in one direction only:
a staggered panel not in this list fails as a new regression, and a panel
in this list that lines up fails as a stale record. With the list empty,
only the first of those can fire, which is the state the ticket was for.
Two panels are never reached by this assertion and are not exemptions
hiding here: `carousel`, whose settings column sits BESIDE the chrome
(a side-by-side column is its own lattice, and the check names the skip
on every run), and the heading / floating-image chromes, which are
flowing bars rather than lattice columns on purpose and carry no
`.builder-module-chrome` strip at all. Both are written down in
docs/UI_RULES.md rather than left to a CSS comment.
